figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of ConceptFormer. The left panel illustrates a case where the standard InfoNCE method fails to find fine-grained local evidence, whereas ConceptFormer retrieves the relevant page. The right panel shows how ConceptFormer allocates adaptive latent concepts from query-related regions and learns them with retrieval-guided representation learning.

Table 1: Overall performance of ConceptFormer. We report Recall@10 and NDCG@10 as evaluation metrics. †, ‡, and § indicate statistically significant improvements over NV-Embed†, VisRAG-Ret‡, and VDocRetriever§, respectively.

Figure 2: 3D retrieval geometry of concept representations. We compare visual and textual concept proxies with ConceptFormer latent concepts using query discriminability, page discriminability, and retrieval alignment.

Table 2: Ablation study of latent concept representation learning in ConceptFormer. † and ‡ indicate statistically significant improvements over ConceptFormer (Text)†, ConceptFormer w/o KL Loss‡, respectively.
Table 3: Sensitivity to the weight 𝜆 of alignment loss Lalign (Eq. 17). All models are implemented using Qwen2.5-vl.
Figure 4: Case study. Regions with higher color intensity indicate stronger patch-level query relevance.
Table 7: Main training and inference configurations of ConceptFormer.
Figure 5: Prompt templates used in Evidence Extraction.
Table 8: Public checkpoints used for baseline evaluation. All identifiers refer to Hugging Face model repositories.
